data.name: सतिश
data.gender_notes: सतिश is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name सतिश is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘सत्य’ (Satya) which means truth. It is a name bestowed upon a child who is believed to bring harmony, satisfaction, and truth to the lives of those around them. In Hindu mythology, the deity Satish is revered as a form of Lord Vishnu, the preserver of the universe. The name सतिश carries the meaning “Truth, Satisfaction” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose सतिश usually hope their child will grow to embody truth, satisfaction and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Brings harmony, satisfaction, and truth to the lives of those around him.
data.etymology: सतिश belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Truth, Satisfaction.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of सतिश total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name सतिश (Satish) holds significant cultural value in Hindu societies as it is derived from the esteemed Sanskrit word 'सत्य' (Satya), which symbolizes truth, integrity, and righteousness. This name bestows a sense of responsibility and moral strength upon the bearer, inspiring them to uphold these virtues in their actions and interactions with others.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Satish is deeply rooted in Hinduism as it represents the divine quality of 'truth'. As a form of Lord Vishnu, Satish serves as a powerful guardian of virtue and dharma. Possessing this name is believed to grant the individual a deeper sense of inner peace, self-awareness, and a connection to deeper spiritual truths. The name inspires one to live a life rooted in truth, honesty, and compassion, ultimately elevating one's consciousness and allowing them to become a beacon of spiritual growth and wisdom for their community.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sati means truth and faith. It represents the inner quality of being steadfast and unwavering, rooted in the eternal truth. Sati is the embodiment of devotion and commitment to one's dharma.

historical_references.reference: Sati, the wife of Lord Shiva, self-immolated herself on his pyre during his funeral. This act of devotion is celebrated as 'Sati' in the Hindu religion.

Sati, a queen of the ancient kingdom of Mahabharata, was the mother of Bhishma Pitamaha. She practiced severe austerities to obtain a divine weapon for her husband, Bhishma, and was known for her devotion and sacrifice.
